content: <p>Tina Gellie has worked for <em>Decanter</em> since 2008 across a number of editorial roles and is currently the brand's Content Director. An awarded wine writer and editor, she won several scholarships on the way to getting her WSET Diploma, and is a freeman of The Worshipful Company of Distillers. She has worked in wine publishing since 2003, including as Deputy Editor and Acting Editor of <em>Wine International</em>. Before her wine career she was a newspaper journalist for broadsheets in London and Australia.</p>

content: <p>Richard Baudains was born and brought up on the formerly French-speaking island of Jersey (hence the French surname). He moved to Italy to teach, and had the good fortune to pursue the profession in many of Italy&#39;s top wine regions. His first article with Decanter was published in 1988, and he has been writing about Italian wine for the magazine ever since, currently with a monthly column on Decanter Premium. He is a judge and long-time regional chair at the Decanter World Wine Awards, on the editorial team of the Slow Wine Guide for Friuli Venezia Giulia, and has taught MA courses on Wine Journalism at the Università delle Scienze Gastronomiche. Baudains judges in wine competitions and leads tastings and educational seminars in various Italian regions. Outside of wine, he works as a Cambridge University English language examiner. He lives in Gorizia.  </p>

title: At the edge of possibility: Africa’s highest vineyards taking shape in Rwanda
content: <p>Malu Lambert DipWSET is a multi-award winning wine writer and critic. She was named Mont Blanc Emerging Wine Writer of the Year at the Louis Roederer International Wine Writers’ Awards in 2019 and won Veritas Young Wine Writer of the Year in 2015. As co-author of <em>Klein Constantia: The Home of Vin de Constance</em>, she received a 2023 OIV Award in Paris. Most recently she was a finalist for the Gusbourne Estate Award for Long-Form Writing at the inaugural 67 Pall Mall Global Wine Communicator Awards (2024). At home in South Africa Malu is a contributing editor for <em>House & Garden</em> and writes regularly for <em>House & Leisure</em>, <em>Winemag</em>, <em>Inside Guide</em> and other local titles. Globally, her work has appeared in <em>Jancis Robinson</em>, <em>Decanter</em>, <em>The Buyer</em>, <em>Falstaff</em>, <em>Drinks International</em>, <em>The Telegraph</em> and <em>Club Oenologique</em>. A seasoned judge, Malu is a taster for <em>Platter’s Wine Guide</em> and she has judged for Decanter, IWSC and Concours Mondial.</p>

These days, his love of wine commonly tests his budgeting skills.</p><p>Beyond wine, Chris also has an MSc in food policy and has a particular interest in sustainability issues. He has also been a food judge at the UK’s Great Taste Awards.</p></div>

title: The smart buyer's guide to... NZ Pinot Noir
content: <div class="author-description"><p>Following a Diploma of Viticulture and Winemaking, Emma Jenkins achieved the Master of Wine qualification in 2011, becoming the ninth New Zealander to do so. She is a wine consultant and also writes for several wine publications, including <i>The Independent Wine Monthly </i>which she co-edits with Jane Skilton MW. A former judge at the Decanter World Wine Awards, Jenkins also judges at other local and international competitions. She teaches Wine and Spirit Education Trust courses and is the Master of Wine Research Paper Chair.</p></div>

title: Malta: Its hidden and historic wine story
content: <p>Sylvia Wu is Decanter's Regional Editor for Asia and Northern & Eastern Europe. She also works as the Editor of Decanter China platforms, overseeing Decanter’s China-focused editorial operation. Trained as a journalist at Beijing Foreign Studies University and the University of Leicester, Sylvia is fluent in English, Japanese and Mandarin. </p><p>After a career in advertising, she began her journey in wine with Decanter in 2012. A former non-drinker, she was immediately drawn to the astonishingly complex yet fascinating world of wine.</p><p>Now Decanter’s ‘Discovery’ Regional Editor, Sylvia is passionate about uncovering lesser-known stories beyond the classic regions and unearthing hidden gems in the wine world, while continuing to deliver Decanter’s editorial content to the Chinese-speaking wine community. She has completed her studies towards the WSET Diploma and Sake Level 3, and is a WSET-qualified educator.</p>

title: Born in the USA: Finding regional identity in American single malt whiskey
summary: This blossoming whiskey category is already showing local character. Susannah Skiver Barton explores how regionality is shaping American single malts, with a region-by-region guide – and six great bottles to try.
content: <p>A veteran journalist and seasoned critic, Susannah Skiver Barton writes about whisky and spirits from around the world. Bylines include <em>The New York Times</em>, <em>Bon Appétit</em>, <em>Imbibe</em>, <em>Food &amp; Wine</em>, <em>Whisky Magazine</em>, <em>VinePair</em>, <em>PUNCH</em>, and more. She is a Certified Spirits Specialist and recipient of the 2020 Alan Lodge Young International Drinks Writer Award. More at <a href="http://susannahskiverbarton.com/" target="_blank">susannahskiverbarton.com</a>.</p>
